# Rung U: the unsigned helpers, UnsignedLong's three, NN64's prefix DOTMINUS and NN32's CHOOSE

## 1. What changed and why

The commits, on `wip/rung-natives-unsigned` from `97a416b18`: `e38365e40` the tests first; `114e35c29` the fix; `776a4e5d9` the two tests of the rewrite's limits; the commit of this report and `record.md`.

The planner's `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/rung-U.patch`, applied as it stands (`git apply`, one warning for the file's own space-then-tab indent at `simpleUnsignedLongArith.java:114`):

- `simpleUnsignedLongArith.unsignedLongToString` prints by `Long.toUnsignedString` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleUnsignedLongArith.java:23-25`), where it printed `Long.toString`, so 2^63 printed `-9223372036854775808`; `unsignedLongWrappingNeg` answers `-a` (`:113-115`), where it answered `a`; the new `unsignedLongToDouble` (`:27-32`), right after `unsignedLongToString`, answers an unsigned long's nearest double: a value at or above 2^63 is halved with its low bit kept as a sticky bit, converted and doubled, which rounds to nearest, ties to even, as walk's `Unsigned.toDouble` does. These compute as walk's `UnsignedLong$ToString`, `$WrappingNegate` and `$AsFloat` (`interpreter/glue/prim/UnsignedLong.java:251-261`, `:365-369`).
- `FNN32`'s `toString` and `asString` print by `Integer.toUnsignedString` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`), and `FNN64`'s `toString` by `Long.toUnsignedString` (`FNN64.java:20`). `FNN32.asString` shadows the prelude's masking getter (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:759`), so it is the half of row 326 that a compiled `NN32` reaches; the prelude's `NN64` getter calls the fixed helper (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:825`).
- `BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.transfer` gives an argument declared `UnsignedLong`, walk's object of `NN64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:475`), the `NN64` argument transfer (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:189-192`). In `value object UnsignedLong` the rewrite gives `self` the owner's name as its declared type (`:124-127`), so without the condition the checker read `self` as `UnsignedLong` against the helper's `long`, read as `ZZ64`, and refused the three bindings (row 873).
- Five strings move from glue classes onto helpers: `UnsignedLong`'s `asString` and `asExprString` onto `unsignedLongToString` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:478-481`) and its `asFloat`, declared at `RR64` as rung A declares the other five (fork 3), onto `unsignedLongToDouble` (`:482-483`); trait `NN64`'s prefix `DOTMINUS` onto `unsignedLongWrappingNeg` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:936-937`); value object `NN32`'s `CHOOSE` onto `simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntOverflowingChoose` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:448-449`), which reaches `simpleLongArith.longOverflowingChoose`, fixed by climb batch 24's rung K.

So 178 of the 449 live bindings name a helper on this tree, 173 on the base: `grep -c '"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers'` of `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss` gives 76 and 97 at `97a416b18`, 77 and 101 at `HEAD`. Of the 82 bindings over `NN32`, `NN64` and `Char` that F-308 counts, four of the six left on glue classes move (`NN32`'s `CHOOSE`, `UnsignedLong`'s two string getters, `NN64`'s prefix `DOTMINUS`); `UnsignedLong`'s `asFloat`, outside the 82, moves too; `NN32`'s `asFloat` (rung A) and `Char`'s `asExprString` (row 861) stay. ## 2. The tests, the failing run and the passing run

Written before the edit and committed in `e38365e40`:

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The helpers are `nativeHelpers/`, which both paths call (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`, B.12); the printing is the compiled run time's (`compiler/runtimeValues/`, B.11); the transfer is the rewrite at the compiled path's parse (`compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java`, F-298); the strings are the one library's (`library.md`, "Designing a change": a native is a public static method of `nativeHelpers/` bound by `builtinPrimitive`).

The precedents, counted in their files:

- The wrapping negation: of the four helper classes with one, three answer `-a`, `simpleIntArith.intWrappingNeg` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java:244-246`), `simpleLongArith.longWrappingNeg` (`simpleLongArith.java:219-221`) and `simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntWrappingNeg` (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:101-103`); `simpleUnsignedLongArith.unsignedLongWrappingNeg` was the one that answered `a`. - The printing: `simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntToString` masks into a `long` (`:31-33`); the run-time classes `FNN32` and `FNN64` were the two that printed signed.
- The transfer: of `transfer`'s three conditions (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:183-192`), the `Char` one reads two names of one carried type (`Char` in the one library, `Character` in the compiler's prelude); the `UnsignedLong` condition is the second such, read at an argument only.

(`test stringifyChars`; row 823) (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-25.md:375-385; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5795-5796, :2029-2030, :2897-2899 at 97a416b18)

## 1. What changed, and why

Three changes in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, and one helper that the second needs, nothing else of the original tree:

- `generateTypeReference`, its `AnyType` branch (base `:5795-5796`, now `:5845-5851`): it was empty and fell through to the throw 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (base `:5802`). It now calls `generateTypeReference` with Any's own name, `NodeFactory.makeId(span, WellKnownNames.anyTypeLibrary(), WellKnownNames.anyTypeName)`, and no static arguments, and continues, as the `TraitType` branch does for a trait (`:5835-5837`). For a name without static arguments the method emits `GETSTATIC <its RTTI class>.ONLY` (`:5759-5767`), here `fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, the field that the bootstrap class declares (`ProjectFortress/src/fortress/AnyType.java`, `RTTIc.ONLY`). The `BottomType`, `SelfType` and `AbbreviatedType` branches stay empty, each still ending in the throw (`:5833-5834`, `:5843-5844`, `:5852-5853`, throw `:5857`).
- `forTry` (base `:2019-2073`, now `:2019-2087`): the throw 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (base `:2029-2030`) is gone. After the catch clauses, which are unchanged, each type of the forbid clause is tested in turn, as a catch clause tests its type (`DUP`, `FException.getValue`, `InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedInstanceOf`, `IFEQ`); on a match the exception's value is passed to `throwForbiddenException`. The rethrow (`ATHROW`) and the label `done` move out of the `if (catchClauses.isSome())` block (`:2041`, `:2078-2081`) and are emitted when the try has a catch clause or a forbid clause, so a try with neither emits what it emitted before.
- `throwForbiddenException` (new, `:2089-2122`): with the exception's value on the stack, it finds `ForbiddenException`'s constructor in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()` (the component's own index when it is that library), takes its parameter type and its result, casts the value to the parameter's class, calls the constructor's static method through `idToPackageClassAndName` and `NamingCzar.jvmMethodDesc`, as a source call of `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted, wraps the result in an `FException` as `forThrow` does (`NEW`, `DUP_X1`, `SWAP`, `INVOKESPECIAL`) and throws it. The api's own types are named unqualified in its index, so the descriptor is made with the library's api as the default: with the program's api the first run asked for `ForbidClauseCompiled$ForbiddenException.class`, 'Resource not found'. - problem: climb batch 23's fork 12: `Int`'s `asFloat` moved at its header `Float` is refused by the checker, 'Function body has type RR64, but declared return type is Float.' at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:375` (the planner's control, explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-25.md:367-397, "The stages"); PLAN's natives line, explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md:52
- spec: Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:47-49 ("a conversion into RR64 ... is explicit, written asFloat(x) with the method that the library declare on Number"), with Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:290-291 (`abstract asFloat(self): RR64`, "the explicit conversion into %RR64%")
- precedent: the bindings that already name a helper beside these, `Int`'s `asString` (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:370-371) and `Long`'s and `BigNum`'s `asString` (F-307, :380, :567); for the new helpers, `simpleIntArith.intToDouble` (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java:411-413)
- deviation: the declared result is `RR64`, not the team's `Float` (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:241, :374, :383, :396, :570), by fork 3; `longToDouble` sits above the comment "The original Java-like arithmetic operators" (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:27-30), not under it as rung-A.patch put it; the two new helpers' comments say what they compute, not which glue class they copy (simpleLongArith.java:27, simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:30)
- historical: ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:241-242, :374-375, :383-384, :396-397, :570-571; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:27-31; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:30-34

## What changed and why

Five bindings of walk's library move from glue classes onto static helpers of `nativeHelpers/` (P-58), and their declared result goes from walk's float object `Float` to `RR64`, the type of the library's abstract `asFloat` on `Number` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291) and of the specification's text (numbers.tex:49):

| owner | line | was | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RR32` | FortressBuiltin.fss:241 | `asFloat(self): Float`, `RR32$AsFloat` | `asFloat(self): RR64`, `simpleDoubleArith.floatToDouble` |
| `Int` | :374 | `Float`, `Int$AsFloat` | `RR64`, `simpleIntArith.intToDouble` |
| `Long` | :383 | `Float`, `Long$AsFloat` | `RR64`, `simpleLongArith.longToDouble` (new) |
| `NN32` | :396 | `Float`, `NN32$AsFloat` | `RR64`, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntToDouble`, through the rewrite's NN32 transfer (F-308) |
| `BigNum` | :570 | `Float`, `BigNum$AsFloat` | `RR64`, `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.toDouble` (new) |

The two new helpers compute as their glue classes: `simpleLongArith.longToDouble` is `(double) a`, as `Long$AsFloat` (interpreter/glue/prim/Long.java:268-271); `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.toDouble` is `a.doubleValue()`, as `BigNum$AsFloat` (BigNum.java:280-283). The three existing helpers compute as theirs: `intToDouble` `(double) a` as `Int$AsFloat` (Int.java:244-246); `floatToDouble` `(double) f` as `RR32$AsFloat` (RR32.java:390-392); `unsignedIntToDouble` `(double) toLong(a)` (simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:226-228), the unsigned value, as `NN32$AsFloat`'s `Unsigned.toDouble(x)` (NN32.java:257-259). Walk boxes the helper's `double` at the declared `RR64` as the same `Float` object as before (F-303), so no value moves under walk: the walk guard passes on the base and on the edit with the same assertions.

I took rung-A.patch's text as it is in the library file, all five headers and strings; in the two Java files I kept its two helpers and their bodies and changed two things: their comments, and the place of `longToDouble`. The patch's comments named the glue class each helper copies ("as walk's Long$AsFloat computes it"); the glue classes go at the switch-over (F-32), so each comment now says what the helper computes ("the nearest double, ties to even", and for `ZZ` "an infinity past the double range"), which the guards assert. The patch put `longToDouble` under the comment "// The original \"Java-like\" arithmetic operators", which heads the arithmetic section that begins at `longAdd`; it is a conversion, so it now sits right above that comment, still right before `longAdd` in the class's order of methods and at the place fork 2 gives (before the addition helper), with no other helper between. Neither change moves a line that rungs R or N write (R writes right after the division helper, N at the class's end, fork 2).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The binding is the library's (`FortressBuiltin.fss`), its helper the compiled path's helper class of its number type (fork 2; explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md, B.12 "Natives"). The library's own way is P-58's bare form, `builtinPrimitive("<class>.<method>")`, as 173 bindings already take it (F-299). Precedent: climb batch 24's small rest (F-307), which moved `Long`'s and `BigNum`'s `asString` onto `longToString` and `toString` beside these; in the same file 97 lines named `nativeHelpers` on the base and 102 after (`grep -c nativeHelpers ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, on `git show 97a416b18:` and on the tree).

The ways the language and the library offer, for the declared result:
1. `RR64`, the type of `Number`'s abstract `asFloat` (FortressLibrary.fsi:291) and of numbers.tex:49: taken (fork 3).
2. `Float`, kept, with a helper answering walk's `Float`: no Java type is read by the checker as `Float`, so a static helper over plain Java values cannot answer it (fork 3; F-303).
3. `Float`, kept, the binding left on its glue class: leaves the five off P-58 and the compiled path, as PLAN's natives line left them.

## What the specification settles

numbers.tex:47-49 says the conversion into `RR64` is explicit, written `asFloat(x)` "with the method that the library declare on Number", and Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:290-291 declares it `abstract asFloat(self): RR64`. The five now answer that type. The specification says nothing of the rounding; the helpers round to nearest, ties to even, as Java's conversions do and as the glue classes did, and the guards assert it at 2^53 + 1 and the `ZZ64` maximum. A `ZZ` past the double range answers an infinity, as `BigNum$AsFloat` did; the specification does not say otherwise (grep -n 'asFloat' Specification/basic-lib/*.tex: numbers.tex:49 only).
